question: Can a shell-fixed bipyramid-symmetric isometry transfer all old-only stock to new-only coordinates and select a gate?
assumptions: 20 shared shell amplitudes pointwise fixed at event, a stronger condition than fixed shell geometry
Linear jump from three old-only to seven new-only oriented simplex coordinates
S3 base permutations, optionally apex C2, act by signed orientation
Unit Q165 metric; real algebraic extension used only for conditional two-memory construction
physical_mapping: OPEN: no source-selected event register, memory, local jump current, physical clock, charge, friction or material port
target_exposure: No measured target or fit; snapped 2→3 geometry and prior gate counterexample already known

result: Every base S3-equivariant linear map from old-only Q^3 to new-only Q^7 has rank≤1. Apex exchange leaves a one-dimensional intertwiner; two old apex-even channels have no new-only image. A conditional real algebraic two-memory jump attains isometry, but neither memory nor gate is source-selected.
